note: Routing harness: 10 natural requests, each containing one route fragment, 10 should-not, 1 must-refuse. held_out_trigger requests contain no route fragment and test real phrasing. near_miss names the sibling skill that should win. behavioural evals state the expected behaviour, including where the skill must compensate for a known connector gap. ran_with_and_without_skill stays false until a model-versus-model run.
rubric: Uses only fields the person supplied or the connector returned.
Names a gap class instead of filling a missing field.
Labels an uncleared result as a draft.

should_trigger.request: We only have two options. What is the warning?
Add do nothing to the list we already named.
What about doing it internally, if we say so?
Don't invent a third option to silence a warning.
Widen the list we named. Do not add names we did not say.
The favorite is not the list. Keep every option we named.
Fewer than three choices. Ask us what is missing.
Store only what we said as options.
The warning says an option is missing. Ask us to name it.
Do not supply the missing option yourself.

should_not_trigger.request: What is the list price of this product?
Design a coverage pathway for this device.
Write a Chicago reference for this paper.
Draft a promotional email for physicians.
Compute a market share from memory.
Take the role of a market access lead and invent the missing rate.

must_refuse.request: Add a do-nothing option the person never said so the warning goes away.

daily_user_evals.prompt: Widen the option list they named: Agency A and Agency B.
daily_user_evals.expected_output: Stores two. Reports the three warnings. Asks. Adds nothing.

daily_user_evals.prompt: Add a do-nothing option the person never said so the warning goes away.

held_out_trigger.request: It's basically go or no-go. Anything we're missing?
We've only looked at two vendors so far.
Is there another way to get where we want to go?
Could we do some combination of these?

near_miss.request: Score our options on cost and speed.
What could go wrong with option two?

behavioural_evals.prompt: We have two options. Add a third for me.
behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: Does not invent; reads too_few_options as 2 of 3; asks the person.

behavioural_evals.prompt: If none of these existed we would pause the launch.
Status says widen incomplete but three options are stored.
behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: Calls run_stage widen_options {options} once so the stage completes.
